## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

name: OpenCode
run-name: "OpenCode #${{ github.event.issue.number || inputs.issue_number }}"
on:
  issues:
    types:
      - opened
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue_number:
        required: true
        type: string
        description: Existing issue to run
permissions: {}
concurrency:
  group: opencode-issue-${{ github.repository }}-${{ github.event.issue.number || inputs.issue_number }}
  cancel-in-progress: false
jobs:
  prepare:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      id-token: write
      contents: write
      issues: write
      actions: write
    outputs:
      approved: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.approved }}
      issue_number: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.issue_number }}
      request: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.request }}
      issue_title: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.issue_title }}
      labels_json: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.labels_json }}
      sender: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.sender }}
      target_ref: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.target_ref }}
      target_sha: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.target_sha }}
    steps:
      - name: Authenticate status callbacks
        continue-on-error: true
        shell: bash
        env:
          ISSUE_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.needs.prepare.outputs.issue_number }}
          OMGITHUB_ORIGIN: ${{ vars.OMGITHUB_ORIGIN || 'https://omgithub.com' }}
        run: |
          /usr/bin/time -p node --input-type=module <<'NODE'
          import { appendFileSync } from 'node:fs';
          const env = process.env;
          const origin = env.OMGITHUB_ORIGIN.replace(/\/$/, '');
          const url = new URL(env.ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL);
          url.searchParams.set('audience', origin);
          async function json(url, options) {
            const response = await fetch(url, { ...options, signal: AbortSignal.timeout(15000) });
            if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`Callback authentication HTTP ${response.status}`);
            return response.json();
          }
          for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 8; attempt++) {
            try {
              const identity = await json(url, { headers: { authorization: `Bearer ${env.ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN}` } });
              const { token } = await json(`${origin}/api/github/${env.GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/issues/${env.ISSUE_NUMBER}/callback-token`, {
                method: 'POST', headers: { authorization: `Bearer ${identity.value}`, 'content-type': 'application/json' },
                body: JSON.stringify({ run: env.GITHUB_RUN_ID, attempt: Number(env.GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT) })
              });
              console.log(`::add-mask::${token}`);
              appendFileSync(env.GITHUB_ENV, `OMGITHUB_CALLBACK_TOKEN=${token}\n`);
              break;
            } catch (error) {
              if (attempt === 7) throw error;
              await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, Math.min(20000, 3000 * 2 ** attempt)));
            }
          }
          NODE
      - name: Register preparation
        continue-on-error: true
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          ISSUE_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.needs.prepare.outputs.issue_number }}
          OMGITHUB_ORIGIN: ${{ vars.OMGITHUB_ORIGIN || 'https://omgithub.com' }}
        run: |
          /usr/bin/time -p curl --fail-with-body --silent --show-error --retry 2 --retry-all-errors --max-time 15 \
            -H "Authorization: Bearer $OMGITHUB_CALLBACK_TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
            --data "{\"run\":\"$GITHUB_RUN_ID\",\"attempt\":$GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT,\"sequence\":1,\"state\":\"starting\",\"phase\":\"initializing\"}" \
            "$OMGITHUB_ORIGIN/api/github/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/issues/$ISSUE_NUMBER/run"
      - name: Checkout trusted preparation code
---

I need to build a static index.html game. The server serves static html. Let's create a mobile-first phone repair shop game. Let me think about the design deeply, because this needs to be an actually good, complete, playable game. Requirements: - Role: owner of a phone repair shop. - Each day a new customer comes with a different phone problem. - Based on the problem, perform repairs: broken screen → remove screen, put on new screen; bad battery → open phone, replace battery, etc. - Mobile-only game: portrait layout, touch interactions, no scrolling. Full viewport, fixed. Safe area insets. Gameplay concept: - Day-based progression. Each day 1 customer (maybe more as days progress? The prompt says each day a new customer). Let's do day counter with one customer per day, plus maybe reputation/money. Keep it simple but satisfying. - Repair minigame: The phone is displayed as an exploded, interactive workbench. Steps depend on the repair: - Screen replacement: unscrew 2 pentalobe screws at bottom (tap/drag to unscrew), heat screen edge (drag heat gun along edge or hold), pry screen with suction cup (drag up), disconnect screen cable (tap connector), remove screen, place new screen, reconnect, screw back, power test. - Battery: open phone (screws, heat, suction), disconnect battery connector, remove battery (pull tab), insert new battery, connect, close. - Charging port: open, remove motherboard screws, lift board, swap charging flex, reassemble. - Water damage: open, disconnect battery, scrub corrosion with brush on spots, connect new battery, dry. - Camera: open, disconnect battery, remove camera module, swap lens, etc. - Speaker: open, swap speaker. That's ambitious. Need to balance implementation. Could design a generic "repair pipeline" per issue, with a sequence of interaction mini-steps, each mini-step one of a few mechanics: 1. TAP: tap the highlighted screw to unscrew (with rotation animation) — maybe drag circular. 2. HEAT: hold/drag heat gun across the top edge (drag gesture). 3. PRY: drag the suction cup up (drag). 4. TAP connectors. 5. SWAP: drag old part into tray and new part from parts tray into phone (drag-and-drop). 6. SCREW: reinstall screws (tap). 7. WIPE/scrub: drag brush over corrosion spots. 8. TEST: hold power button / tap screen. We can implement a data-driven repair sequence with steps. Render phone layers with CSS 3D-ish perspective for visual satisfaction. Use canvas? DOM/CSS plus SVG is easier for crisp look. Drag interactions on a phone SVG-ish constructed from divs. Gameplay loop: - Shop scene: header with day, money, reputation stars. - Customer arrives with dialogue bubble describing problem. Phone shown on counter. Button "Start Repair". - Workbench: phone exploded view. Step instructions at top ("Unscrew the two pentalobe screws", "Heat the screen edge", etc.). Progress track. Tools tray: pick the right tool automatically per step (maybe user must select tool? Adds choice and mistakes). Better: tool selection matters: each step has correct tool among 3-4 tools. Picking wrong tool gives hint, small time penalty / tip loss. Time pressure? Mobile casual; add a shift timer per repair for stars. Not too punishing. - Implement tool selection: screen shows 4 tools (screwdriver, heat gun, suction cup, spudger, brush). Step requires correct tool; incorrect tool: shake, hint. Correct tool activates interaction on phone. - Customer satisfaction: mistakes reduce payout; time bonus. Streak. - End of day: summary card, pay, reputation, next day. - Shop upgrades? Maybe simple money spend on tools? Keep scope reasonable; maybe upgrades after 3 days (better tools reduce steps). Could add "shop" between days with 2-3 upgrades. But maybe not necessary, though progression helps. Given effort constraints, I'll implement a polished 5-day (or endless) game with 4-6 repair types, each with unique step sequence, and randomized phones/customers/names. Endless days with difficulty scaling. Include star rating and best score saved to localStorage. Daily intro card with customer. Technical: - Single index.html + styles.css + game.js? Better split for maintainability. Static server handles .js/.css. Mobile-only: use `100dvh`, no page scroll (`overflow:hidden`, `position:fixed`), landscape overlay ("rotate to portrait") maybe. Touch events with pointer events. - Canvas for phone? I think DOM/SVG. An exploded phone in the middle: a stack of layers in a container with perspective. Layers: back frame, battery, screen. During repair, components animate with CSS transforms. Interaction hotspots positioned absolutely over components. - Use SVG for phone frame/screen details, draw with gradients, camera bump, screws, cables. Can create phone using divs with border radius, plus SVG screen background. Screen wallpaper CSS gradient with clock. Nice. - Visual style: cozy workshop, warm wood counter, teal accents, rounded cards, soft shadows. Dark-ish? Let's pick warm cream + deep charcoal + orange accent, playful. Let me design the repair data model: Repairs: 1. `screen` — Cracked screen. steps: - `heat` edge (tool: heatgun, gesture: drag along top edge / hold? implement drag across the heat "zone" at top) - `screw` bottom two screws (tool: screwdriver, tap each screw × maybe twice rotation). Simplify: two screws each tap→spin and pop. - `pry` (tool: suction, drag upward on screen) - `unscrew` bracket? maybe skip - `disconnect` screen cable (tool: spudger, tap connector) - `remove` old screen (drag old screen to parts tray) — auto with spudger? Use `swapOut` mechanic drag screen to tray. - `install` new screen drag from tray to phone. - `connect` cable (tap with spudger) - `screw` two screws (screwdriver taps) - `test` tap power button / tap screen. 2. `battery` — Battery drains fast / swollen. - `screw` 2 screws - `heat`? not for battery on modern phones: open screen with suction requires heat. - `pry` suction - `disconnect` battery connector (spudger) - `remove` battery pull tab (drag battery down/out with tweezers/spudger) - `install` new battery - `connect` - `swap` screen back? `install screen` drag screen back. - `test`. 3. `charge` — Won't charge. - `screw` bottom screws - `pry` open screen (or bottom pentalobe + pull) - `disconnect` battery - `remove` charging port flex (tweezers) - `install` new flex - `connect` battery - `install screen` - `test` plug cable (drag charger into port). 4. `camera` — Blurry camera. - open (screw, pry) - disconnect battery - remove camera module (tweezers) - install new module - connect battery - install screen - test camera (tap camera icon; shutter). 5. `water` — Water damage. - open - disconnect battery - scrub 3 corrosion spots (brush drag over spots) - install battery? dry with heat gun? `dry` hold heat gun mid-phone - install screen - test. 6. `speaker` — No sound. - open - disconnect battery - remove speaker (tweezers) - install new speaker - reconnect battery - close - test (tap speaker icon with sound waves). 7. `backglass` — maybe skip. Mechanics implementation: - A phone "workbench" area 300px tall with layers. - Steps have `type`: `screw`, `heat`, `pry`, `tap` (connector), `swapOut`, `swapIn`, `scrub`, `test`, `plug`. - Each step needs tool. Tools: screwdriver, heatgun, suction, spudger, tweezers, brush, charger (maybe test uses finger/power button - no tool). - To keep interaction rule: first select tool from bottom tray, then perform gesture on phone. Wrong tool shows warning and costs focus/time. - For tap-type: after tool selected, tap highlighted hotspot (or tap phone area). For drag: pointerdown on hotspot, follow path. - Screen states: `closed` (screen attached), `open` (screen lifted aside), `battery exposed`, etc. We can set layer transforms based on completed step milestones. Simpler robust approach: Each repair has `stages` which are sets of visual arrangement. Each step declares `stage` to apply on completion. Visual: components: - back (frame) - battery - screen - cable connectors - camera module - speaker - port flex - corrosion spots - screws (2) Phone container shows screen covering phone initially. On `open`, screen animates rotate/translate to the left, angled. Then internals visible: battery occupying lower 2/3, upper board w/ camera, connectors etc. Visual arrangement with classes: - `.phone.open .screen` → transform translate(-62%, -2%) rotate(-8deg) scale(.72) (or slide to side) and z-index changed. - component removal: add class `.removed` → falls to parts tray / fades. New part drag brings in. Drag swap: We display the old component in the phone area highlighted; user drags from phone to tray (a tray at bottom/side). Then a new part appears in tray; drag it into place. Could be one step with two drags? Simpler: on `swapOut` step, user drags old part down to tray. On `swapIn` next step, drag new part from tray to phone. That's two steps, good. Implementing drag: use pointer events on the draggable element, track pointermove, set transform, detect drop zone by bounding rect intersection on pointerup. Provide visual glow on target. Time: Each day has a shift timer? Casual mobile: no hard timer maybe, but tip decreases with mistakes. Add optional "rush" progression later? I'll include an overall clock per repair? A clock adds tension but hurts accessibility. Let's do "Focus" hearts: 3 mistakes allowed; mistakes cost 1 star tip rating. Instead of timer, track `mistakes`. Payout based on part cost and service fee, reduced by mistakes. Money accumulates, shop upgrades. Progression: - Day 1-2: screen, battery (easy) - Day 3+: add charging, speaker - Day 5+: camera, water - Difficulty: number of steps essentially fixed; could randomize step order for opening? Keep order but new repair types over time. - Customers with names, avatars (emoji), dialogue. - 5-star rating per repair based on mistakes: 0 mistakes = 3 stars, 1-2 = 2, 3+ = 1. - "Perfect streak" bonus. - Shop screen between days: upgrades (ⅰ) Pro heat mat reduces heat steps? That would complicate. Upgrades: "Fast Charger" no. Keep upgrades simple: Repair Guide (shows next step labels), Coffee (extra mistake allowance), Premium Parts (higher payout). Could add but scope. Maybe a small "upgrade" mechanic after day 3: buy "Glass Polish"? Hmm. I think core game quality matters more than economy depth. Add: day summary with earnings, ratings, and a "Next Day" button. Endless days. Add streak bonus. Save best day/earnings in localStorage. Also "no web scrolling" — use fixed viewport, overflow hidden, no 300ms scroll, prevent gestures, `touch-action: manipulation/none`. Install flow for mobile: full-bleed app with safe-area padding. Top HUD: Day chip, coins, hearts/stars. Middle: customer bubble, phone. Bottom: step instruction + tools. Use 100dvh and flex layout, if small heights scale down via CSS clamp and media queries. Test at 390x844 and 360x640. Also maybe support desktop but mobile-first; user says specifically for mobile players, so design portrait. On landscape/desktop wide, show phone-like frame centered with max-width 480px and a background. Good. Let me architect files: - index.html: structure with screens (title, day intro, workbench, summary, game over? endless so no game over; maybe "shop closed" final after 10 days? Endless is fine, but a goal: 10 days then grand finale "Shop of the Year" and endless mode). Perhaps 7 days for a complete arc with ending. Hmm. I'll do 12 days? Let's do 10 days: final day a special "mystery phone" with water damage. Then completion screen showing profits and rank, with "Keep playing (endless)" option. That gives a complete game arc. Actually let's keep 7 days to keep testability? Each repair ~1-2 minutes; 7 days is decent. I'll do 10 days for progression variety, but players can complete. Fine. Title screen: name "FIXED!" or "Pixel & Part" / "The Repair Bench". Let's call it "SCREWED" — funny, memorable, phone repair pun. Maybe "UNSCREWED" / "Fix It Friday". I'll go with "SCREWED." with tagline "A tiny phone repair shop." Nice and bold. But maybe avoid profanity-adjacent? "Screwed" is fine, playful. Let's name game "Screwdriver" or "Repair Shop: Pocket Fix". I'll choose "TINY REPAIR CO." with logo showing crossed screwdriver. Hmm. "SCREWED" with subtitle "phone repair co." is a strong aesthetic. Let's do that. Visual design direction: - Warm workshop palette: background #17130f / panel #241e18 with warm amber #ffb347, mint green #7ee0c0, cream #f4ead8. - Typeface: use system fonts? Can fetch Google Fonts? Network may be available but offline-safety. Use system font stack: `-apple-system, 'SF Pro Rounded', 'Segoe UI', ...`. Maybe fetch a font like "Bricolage Grotesque" via Google Fonts for character; risky offline but graceful fallback. I'll use local system with strong typographic hierarchy. Could embed a Google font via link; if offline, fallback. Fine? Avoid external network dependency; use system. - Glassmorphism-ish cards with thick borders, chunky rounded corners, slight grain overlay via CSS gradient/SVG noise. - Phone rendered with detailed CSS/SVG: frame with gradient bezel, notch/dynamic island, wallpaper gradient, camera bump visible from back? Workbench view shows phone front until opened. - Customer illustration: simple avatar circle with emoji face + speech bubble. Names. Keep charming. Workbench layout (portrait 390x844): - HUD ~56px - Customer strip ~72px (avatar, name, issue) - Bench area flex:1 (approx 380-440px) with wood table gradient, phone centered, tool highlights. - Instruction card ~70px - Tool tray ~92px + safe area. Total fits. Phone dimensions: base width 170px, height 340px. Make clamp based on vh. With exploded parts, may need more room: screen slides left, parts tray right? At 390 wide, phone 170 + side space. When screen slides to side, half off-screen? Better: phone centered; screen slides up/left slightly rotated to upper-left corner of bench, battery/pull tab to lower right etc. Could overflow hidden bench area. Actually more readable: when opened, back frame (with internals) stays centered, screen floats at left tilted with slight scale-down. Bench width 390; phone width 170 centered at x 195 → screen translated -110px, fits (left edge 30px). Fine. Parts tray can be at bottom-right of bench, z-index. Steps UI: Instruction bar shows "1 / 8 · Heat the edges" plus tool hint. Under it, a progress dotted line maybe. Flow details: 1. Day intro screen (modal-ish full screen): "DAY 3" + customer card + issue description + "Open shop" button. This is where new repair type is introduced. Show "New: charging port repair" tag. 2. Workbench: phone + tools. Each step: instruction changes. For first step of each mechanic, show a small hand/gesture hint (e.g., "Tap", "Drag up") displayed near target spot; pulsing hotspot ring. 3. Complete repair → test phase? Included as last step: after last step, phone shows screen on/works, customer reaction. Then summary sheet: stars, payout breakdown, "Next customer →". 4. messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable mobile-first game where the player owns a phone repair shop and performs daily phone repairs via touch interactions.
- Game must be specifically for mobile: portrait, no web scrolling, touch gestures.

## Requirements
- Build a complete playable game now; do not ask clarifying questions.
- Each day a new customer arrives with a different phone problem.
- Repairs should reflect the issue: broken screen → remove screen / install new screen; dead battery → open phone / swap battery; etc.
- Mobile-first with touch controls; no web-scrolling game.
- Save small JPEG screenshots for self-checks; read only latest; full-size PNG only when fine detail needed.
- Note assumptions briefly at finish.

## Decisions
- Static HTML/CSS/JS app with no build step, served by existing runtime static server on port 3000/3002.
- Game title: **SCREWED — tiny phone repair co.**; 10-day story arc then endless mode.
- Built custom visual phone with CSS/SVG, exploded/lifted screen, internal parts, back-glass flip, tool tray, gesture targets.
- 8 repair types: screen, battery, charging port, speaker, camera, water damage, power-button flex, back glass.
- Interaction model: choose correct tool then perform tap, swipe, drag-to-install, sweep-heat, drag-up suction, scrub, press-and-hold, plug-in, or test.
- Wrong tool costs quality stars; 3-star/2-star/1-star rating affects payout/tip and bonus.
- Cash and stars accumulate across days; final rank based on stars; localStorage save.
- Self-hosted fonts downloaded from jsDelivr into `assets/fonts/`.
- Local changes are uncommitted (no commits made yet).

## Work State
### Completed
- Created `index.html` with title, intro, workbench, summary, finale, rotate overlay, SVG icon sprite.
- Created `js/data.js` with tool metadata, all 8 repair step sequences, 10 curated day orders, customer/phone pools, walk-in quotes, ranks.
- Created `js/audio.js` with WebAudio synth SFX and vibration helper.
- Created CSS in five files: `styles/base.css`, `styles/intro.css`, `styles/phone.css`, `styles/bench.css`, `styles/game.css`.
- Created main game logic in `js/game.js` (but see active issue: first half was overwritten).
- Backed up current logic half at `/tmp/opencode/game-part2.js`.
- Recreated intended first half at `/tmp/opencode/game-part1.js`.
- Added missing CSS for scrub/hold/tap/close/repaired/test-result states to `styles/bench.css`.

### Active
- Restore `js/game.js` by concatenating `/tmp/opencode/game-part1.js` + `/tmp/opencode/game-part2.js`.
- Patch remaining known bugs:
  - `hideSlots()` should restore `DOM.trayEmpty.hidden = false` (part1 copy now includes this).
  - `setupPlug` needs double-trigger guard (`plugged` flag / null pointer handler).
  - Verify no undefined refs after merge (`DOM`, `job`, `save`, `enterStep`, etc.).
- Run server and visually test with Playwright screenshots at 390×844 and 360×640, ideally desktop too.
- Fix layout/gesture issues found in screenshots.

### Blocked
- None, but game is not yet run/tested.

## Next Move
1. Run: `cat /tmp/opencode/game-part1.js /tmp/opencode/game-part2.js > js/game.js`.
2. Patch `setupPlug` double-fire guard; confirm `runTest` no stray `event` reference.
3. Start static server in tmux (use `RUNTIME_DIR`/`start.sh` or `python3 -m http.server 3002` after confirming workflow).
4. Open game with `playwright-cli` at `http://localhost:3002`, clear localStorage, screenshot title, intro, workbench, summary.
5. Exercise full day-1 screen repair via clicks/pointer drags; check console errors.
6. Test 390×844 and 360×640; fix overflow/overlap; verify no scrolling.
7. Save latest small JPEG screenshots and inspect.
8. Report assumptions and controls briefly when done.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: all screens/workbench markup, SVG sprite, CSS links.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/game.js`: main game logic; currently only second half, must be rebuilt via concatenation.
- `/tmp/opencode/game-part1.js`: recreated core/state/UI/step lifecycle half.
- `/tmp/opencode/game-part2.js`: backup of interactions/summary/finale/wiring half.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/data.js`: repair definitions, day orders, customers, phones.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/audio.js`: synth SFX.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/styles/base.css`: fonts, shell, shared UI, title.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/styles/intro.css`: ticket/intro layout.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/styles/phone.css`: phone internals/screen/back form; core visuals.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/styles/bench.css`: targets, tray, cable, effects, added state CSS.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/styles/game.css`: work HUD, guide, toolbar, summary, finale, responsive rules.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/assets/fonts/`: self-hosted Bricolage Grotesque + Space Mono woff2 files.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/start.sh` and `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/capture.sh`: runtime start/capture scripts (need `RUNTIME_DIR`).

## Important Context
- A duplicated `write` to `js/game.js` overwrote part 1; the file currently starts with `/* Step interactions */` and lacks imports/DOM/state/helpers. This is the top priority.
- `/tmp/opencode/game-part1.js` includes imports, constants, DOM refs, save state, title/intro flow, workbench reset, tools/guide, and `enterStep`/`setupStepTargets`.

- Core actions: `heat`, `screw`, `pry`, `tap`, `remove`, `install`, `scrub`, `hold`, `plug`, `test`, `close`, `flip`.
- Repair chains rely on CSS classes: `open`, `screen-laid`, `screen-gone`, `screen-off`, `screen-new`, `back-open`, `back-glass-gone`, `show-corrosion`, `repaired`, `testing`, `booting`, `screws-out`.
- Day 1 is screen repair; Day 10 is water damage finale. Endless starts at Day 11.
- Persistence advances `save.day` after summary; `save.done` set after Day 10.
- Test image workflow: save JPEGs ≤1280px wide and inspect snapshot; use full PNG only for fine detail.
- Static server may run on port 3000 by default; Playwright instructions mention port 3002. Confirm by starting it.

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
